problem: Mobile balls are too small; graphics settings are absent; a suspended frame driver reports a stall on resume; pocketed balls disappear without a visual return to the player.
reuseDecision: Extend canonical canvas coordinates and captured pointer input. Use native Pointer Events, ResizeObserver and Web Animations; panzoom was reviewed but its independent gesture owner conflicts with cue input. Reuse the existing engine patch hook for a hash-guarded frame-driver lifecycle fix. Shared graphics preferences drive each renderer; domain outcomes alone authorize pot feedback.
nonGoals: Full pyramid rules or online/server hosting
Changing deterministic shot results to match cosmetic animations
Increasing byte budgets or muting genuine frame-loop faults
Copying the generated mockup as a screenshot of working code
acceptance: Every games/**/*.ts file has one architecture owner and all static and dynamic relative imports resolve through declared dependencies
Pocket Club collision, deterministic simulation, immutability, foul, group assignment, scratch, and eight-ball tests pass
The production hub exposes billiards through the Personal Island and ?game=billiards while preserving all existing routes
SolidJS mounts the billiards interface and Canvas 2D renders project-authored table, balls, guide, cue, and responsive controls
The browser contract executes a real break shot, observes movement, waits for rest, and captures every required viewport without runtime errors
The Colyseus adapter remains optional and lazy while billiards.proto preserves a versioned transport-neutral message contract
Ball markings roll over a lit spherical surface according to table displacement rather than rotating as flat discs
Source checks, strict typecheck, production build, bundle ratchet, and all browser contracts pass before publication
The unchanged base/startup bundle ratchet and explicit Pocket Club lazy-client and Colyseus chunk ratchets all pass
Placement confirms exactly once, clears ball-in-hand, hides the solid cue ball and rejects shooting before confirmation in the domain
Click/tap locks aim; mouse and touch pull/forward strokes use fresh projected velocity, reach contact, and cancel safely on capture loss, blur or orientation change
Portrait coordinate round trips, keyboard repeat protection, server turn/revision/sequence authority and disposal races have regression tests
Aim, power, spin, placement and stroke previews travel through direct Colyseus room messages; no prototype patch or no-op adapter remains
Publish only a tested commit and verify the deployed build identity rather than assuming an HTTP 200 is the new build
All previous raw/gzip/Brotli limits remain byte-for-byte unchanged and pass
Extracted CSS is included in total/base byte accounting and loads before the lazy game mounts
Compact engine preparation rejects an unrecognized engine revision, modified entry point or explicit OTA configuration
All four production browser suites and two-client Colyseus integration pass before publishing stable
Russian and American games can coexist without changing global physics; legacy wire snapshots default to American geometry.
The new-game dialog does not reset state until confirmed; cancel and Escape return focus and preserve an in-progress game.
Both presets use the same geometry for rack, placement, collision, preview and visible pockets. Narrow pockets reject oblique shots but accept centered shots.
HUD pots show the actual shooter rather than infer group ownership, including wrong-group and foul pots.
Mobile overview fits all six pockets; automatic aim zoom, two-pointer pan/pinch and reset use the same pointer inverse and cannot accidentally shoot or place a ball.
Camera stops moving during cue gestures, resets on shot/restart/orientation, and respects reduced-motion and auto-zoom preferences.
Graphics menu is keyboard accessible and saved; auto/high/balanced/low affects real renderer quality across routes.
Pocket animations consume semantic pocket events exactly once, preserve shot ownership, exclude cue scratches from HUD rewards and cancel cleanly on restart/unmount.
Frame-driver tests cover tab resume, suspended event loop, genuinely dropped RAF, duplicate generation rejection and balanced ref counts; no watchdog errors are hidden.
Published build has zero overlap between both rollers and shot action on all six viewports; tested source and artifact identity match.
